summary: Task 9 test migration from WebTestClient/Mono → MockMvc/Optional is mechanically clean: every reactive symbol (Mono, Flux, StepVerifier, ReactiveMongoTemplate, MockServerWebExchange, WebTestClient, ReactiveRedisConnectionFactory) is gone from the in-scope tree (verified by grep across webhook/, jobs/, admin/). Coverage of the major invariants — 401 vs 404 anti-enumeration, DuplicateKey self-heal, 413 filter end-to-end + per-branch unit, CAS first-writer-wins outcome, scrubbed rethrow with no cause chain, token-scrubber per-call-site ListAppender filtered by Logger+Level, AC-17b cascade ordering temporal sandwich — is solid and behavior-asserting (no mock-return anti-pattern; ProcessTelegramUpdateJobTest autowires real repos + spies real services). However, three TDD anchors from tasks/9.md are not realized: (a) D14's new file `TelegramWebhookP99IT.java` was not created (the P99 method was removed but never re-extracted), so AC2 (P99 <100ms over 100 parallel POSTs under real transport) is currently untested — this is a hard AC regression; (b) `receive_missingUpdateId_returns400` (TDD anchor for the controller's `extractUpdateId == null → 400` branch) is missing — the controller code path is live but uncovered; (c) `eventWriteBeforeStatusFlip_orderingInvariant` (Mockito InOrder verifier) is absent — the ordering invariant under AC (`event-write completes BEFORE status flip to DONE`) is asserted by neither call-order verification nor any state-driven proxy. The ownerChatId CAS test pins the outcome (chatId stays = 100L) but does not pin the no-throw / no-ERROR-log semantics that the task explicitly calls out. ConcurrencyTestUtils.parallelInvoke is correct (CountDownLatch barrier works as intended; the defensive double-countDown in finally is no-op once latch is at zero), but a minor naming/comment cleanup would help. WebhookSecurityBlockTest has one weak "NOT 403" assertion that would not catch most regressions. Test pyramid balance is healthy (unit filter test + integration controller IT + slice security IT + worker IT). Net: ship-blocking work is the missing P99IT file (D14, AC2); other gaps are major-severity TDD anchor misses that should be added in this task before merge.

findings.issue: D14 + AC line 172 in tasks/9.md explicitly require extracting the P99 latency probe to a NEW file `TelegramWebhookP99IT.java` with `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` + autowired `TestRestTemplate` + `@Tag("slow")` + `ConcurrencyTestUtils.parallelInvoke(100, ...)`. The P99 test was correctly removed from `TelegramWebhookControllerIT` (now MockMvc, where transport overhead is zero and `<100ms` is trivially passed per D14), but the replacement file was never created. `find backend/src/test/java -name 'TelegramWebhookP99IT.java'` returns nothing. Result: AC2 (`webhook P99 latency <100ms` per user-spec) has zero automated verification. The whole point of D14 was to preserve meaningful P99 measurement; deleting the probe without extracting it is a hard AC regression.
findings.recommendation: Create `backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/webhook/TelegramWebhookP99IT.java` per the spec at tasks/9.md lines 116-117 / lines 240-241. Class skeleton: `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT) @AutoConfigureWebTestClient(disabled) @ActiveProfiles("test") @Testcontainers @Tag("slow") class TelegramWebhookP99IT { static MongoDBContainer MONGO_DB; static GenericContainer<?> REDIS; @LocalServerPort int port; @Autowired TestRestTemplate restTemplate; @Test void p99Latency_under100msAt100ParallelRequests() { ... }`. Because `AbstractIntegrationTest` is `WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT` already AND class-level `webEnvironment` is set at the class — actually re-check: `AbstractIntegrationTest` is now `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT) @AutoConfigureMockMvc` so subclasses inherit RANDOM_PORT, BUT MockMvc is still wired. The P99 IT can extend AbstractIntegrationTest, ignore the `mockMvc` field, autowire `TestRestTemplate`, and use real transport. Inside the test method: `ConcurrencyTestUtils.parallelInvoke(100, () -> { long t0 = System.nanoTime(); ResponseEntity<Void> r = restTemplate.postForEntity(URI.create("http://localhost:" + port + "/webhooks/telegram/" + projectId), new HttpEntity<>(jsonBody, headers), Void.class); assertThat(r.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.OK); return System.nanoTime() - t0; })`, sort, `assertThat(latencies.get(98) / 1_000_000).isLessThan(100L)`.

findings.issue: TDD anchor at tasks/9.md line 140 (`...::receive_missingUpdateId_returns400 — body without update_id → 400 empty`) is not present in `TelegramWebhookControllerIT`. The controller code path is live (controller.java rewrite handles `updateId == null → return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build();` with a scrubbed WARN log) but has zero test coverage. Litmus test fail: if the production code accidentally returned 500 (NPE) or 200 (silent drop) instead of 400 on a missing-update_id payload, no test would catch it. Grep on the IT file shows zero `400`, zero `BadRequest`, zero `isBadRequest`, zero `missingUpdateId` references.
findings.recommendation: Add `@Test void receive_missingUpdateId_returns400EmptyBody()` to `TelegramWebhookControllerIT`. Body: `Project p = seedProject(); seedBot(p.getId(), BotStatus.CONNECTED, SECRET_HASH); Document noUpdateId = new Document().append("message", new Document("text", "/start")); int status = doPost(p.getId(), SECRET_PLAIN, noUpdateId); assertThat(status).isEqualTo(400); assertThat(rawUpdateRepository.count()).isZero(); assertThat(enqueuedCount()).isZero();`. Also worth asserting the scrubbed WARN log site exists via the existing `appender` (per AC `scrubber log sites preserved on: ...controller missing-update_id WARN`).

findings.issue: TDD anchor at tasks/9.md line 144 (`eventWriteBeforeStatusFlip_orderingInvariant — InOrder verifier: eventService.logEvent(...) called BEFORE rawUpdateRepository.save with DONE`) is not present. Grep on the file: zero `InOrder`, zero `inOrder`, zero verify-order constructs. Acceptance Criterion at line 166 of tasks/9.md explicitly states `event-write completes BEFORE status flip to DONE (InOrder verifier passes)`. The existing tests verify that AN event is written (eventRepository.count() == 1) AND that processingStatus == DONE at end, but they cannot detect a regression where the status flip is moved to happen BEFORE the event write — both end-state invariants would still hold. Litmus test fail: if a refactor moved `rawUpdateRepository.save(raw with DONE)` to before `eventService.logEvent(...)`, all existing tests pass; audit trail loses ordering guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) switch one test to spy `EventService` + `RawUpdateRepository` and use `InOrder inOrder = inOrder(eventService, rawUpdateRepository); inOrder.verify(eventService).logEvent(any(), any(), any(), any(), any()); inOrder.verify(rawUpdateRepository).save(argThat(r -> r.getProcessingStatus() == RawUpdateStatus.DONE));` — OR (b) keep state-driven style but capture a timestamp inside an event-write spy and assert `event.createdAt < reloadedRawUpdate.updatedAt` (requires `updatedAt` populated on save). Approach (a) is more direct and matches the TDD anchor literally. Add `@MockitoSpyBean EventService eventService` + `@MockitoSpyBean RawUpdateRepository rawUpdateRepositorySpy` (separate from the autowired one used for state assertions) — or wrap the existing autowired beans with Mockito.spy() at runtime. Resulting test fires `/start` payload, runs `job.handle(...)`, then `inOrder.verify(eventService, times(1)).logEvent(...); inOrder.verify(rawUpdateRepository, times(1)).save(argThat(r -> r.getProcessingStatus() == RawUpdateStatus.DONE));`.

findings.issue: Test pins the outcome (`ownerChatId` stays = 100L) but does NOT pin the invariant from tasks/9.md AC line 166 / Edge case 263: 'CAS findAndModify for ownerChatId first-writer-wins (null return treated as benign no-op — do NOT log ERROR, do NOT throw)'. Current test cannot distinguish (a) `findAndModify` returned null AND code silently no-op'd, from (b) `findAndModify` returned null AND code logged ERROR but didn't propagate (still leaves ownerChatId pinned because the save path was never reached), from (c) `findAndModify` was never called because some upstream check short-circuited. Litmus test fail: if a refactor introduced `if (mongoTemplate.findAndModify(...) == null) { log.error("CAS failed!"); throw new IllegalStateException(); }`, the rethrow would tick the failure counter and write FAILED status — but THIS test only asserts the bot's ownerChatId, not the success counter or RawUpdate status of the second invocation.
findings.recommendation: Extend `ownerChatIdPopulate_secondStartDifferentChat_doesNotOverwrite` with two extra assertions: (1) `assertThat(failureCount()).as("CAS predicate-fail must NOT tick failure counter — it is benign").isEqualTo(beforeFailure);` capturing `beforeFailure` BEFORE the second `job.handle(second.getId())`; (2) `assertRawUpdateDone(second.getId())` to prove the second update reached DONE (not FAILED). (3) Assert the ERROR log appender filtered by `Level.ERROR` is empty for the second invocation: `assertThat(jobAppender.list.stream().filter(e -> e.getLevel() == Level.ERROR).toList()).as("CAS predicate-fail must NOT log ERROR").isEmpty();`. Combined, these pin the 'benign no-op' contract literally.

findings.issue: TDD anchor at tasks/9.md line 131 explicitly calls for `multiValueTransferEncoding_caseFold_rejectsWith413` — `Transfer-Encoding: gzip,Chunked` → still 413 (Locale.ROOT fold + substring contains). Edge case at line 271 explains the Turkish-locale JVM dotless-i bug as the reason `Locale.ROOT` is mandatory. Current `chunkedEncoding_rejects413_incrementsCounter` only tests lowercase `chunked`; `warnLogOn413_noTokenInOutput` uses lowercase `chunked, x-...` but does not exercise mixed-case folding. A regression where the filter switched to `.toLowerCase()` (no Locale.ROOT) would pass all current tests on non-Turkish locales and fail in production on a Turkish-locale JVM. A regression where the filter did exact-match `equals("chunked")` instead of `contains` would also pass current tests and fail on the `gzip,chunked` legal HTTP/1.1 multi-value case.
findings.recommendation: Add `@Test void multiValueTransferEncodingCaseFold_rejects413()`. Body: `MockHttpServletRequest req = post("/webhooks/telegram/abc"); req.addHeader(HttpHeaders.TRANSFER_ENCODING, "gzip,Chunked"); MockHttpServletResponse resp = new MockHttpServletResponse(); AtomicBoolean downstream = new AtomicBoolean(false); invoke(req, resp, downstream); assertThat(resp.getStatus()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.value()); assertThat(downstream.get()).isFalse(); assertThat(counter()).isEqualTo(1.0);`. Optionally add a second variant `"GZIP, CHUNKED"` (all-uppercase) to lock in the Locale.ROOT fold.

findings.issue: Both tests assert only `status != 403`. The test name 'reachesController_not403Csrf' is precise, but the assertion is vague — any status in {200, 400, 401, 404, 500} passes. If a regression caused the controller to return 500 due to a NullPointerException, or to return 401 due to a security filter ordering bug, these tests would pass while real bugs hide. The original intent is 'security chain releases the request to the controller'; the current assertion does not pin where the request lands. Litmus test fail: if a buggy filter ordering caused webhook POSTs to return 500 unconditionally, both tests pass.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen: for `postWebhookWithoutAuth_reachesController_not403Csrf`, change to `assertThat(status).isIn(401, 404)` — both prove the controller handled the request (401 = invalid_secret branch with empty header, 404 = project_not_found for the hex ObjectId). For `postWebhookWithoutXsrfToken_doesNot403_scopedCsrfDisableActive`, same `assertThat(status).isIn(401, 404)`. Pinning to a specific status set converts the test from 'detects 403 regression only' to 'detects any deviation from controller-side error paths'.

findings.issue: Test name pins 'EmptyBody' but the assertion only checks status. The happy-path test (line 193) explicitly asserts `result.getResponse().getContentLength()).isZero()` — the 401 path does not. A regression that started returning a JSON body via GlobalErrorHandler on the 401 path (which would violate Decision 3) would pass this test. AC at line 162 of tasks/9.md: 'Explicit-status no-body responses preserved (all error paths return ResponseEntity.status(...).build(), never throw to GlobalErrorHandler).' The 401 path is a critical surface for this AC.
findings.recommendation: Replace `doPost(...)` calls with direct `mockMvc.perform(...).andReturn()` and additionally assert `assertThat(result.getResponse().getContentLength()).isZero();` (or `assertThat(result.getResponse().getContentAsByteArray()).isEmpty();`). Apply the same to `receive_missingProject_returns404EmptyBody_counterTicked` (line 222) and `receive_softDeletedProject_returns404` / `receive_disconnectedBot_returns404` / `receive_malformedObjectId_returns404` / `receive_anotherBotsSecret_returns401`. Five error-path tests should all assert empty body to pin Decision 3.

findings.issue: Mechanism is functionally correct (CountDownLatch.countDown is no-op once count reaches 0, so the duplicate countDown in `finally` is harmless), but the comment at line 34-35 says 'Defensive: countDown also lives in the finally so any exception en route here still releases the caller' — this is misleading because the exception path being defended against (interrupted before `ready.countDown()` on line 36 runs) is unreachable: line 36 is the very first statement in the try block, and the only thing that runs before it is Future.submit machinery which lives in the parent thread. The true defensive value is against an `OutOfMemoryError` or `StackOverflowError` between `ready.countDown()` (L36) and `start.await()` (L37) — which is exotic. The current shape is correct but the comment overstates the defensive value, and a reader may add a second pre-barrier counter or restructure assuming the finally is load-bearing.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) move `ready.countDown()` into `finally` ONLY (the body becomes `try { start.await(); return task.call(); } finally { ready.countDown(); }`) — but then `ready.await()` would block until tasks COMPLETE, not until they park, which inverts the barrier semantics. So (a) is wrong. Keep the current shape, but update the comment to: `// Pre-barrier countDown: signal we are parked. The duplicate countDown in finally is harmless (countDown is monotonic at 0) and exists only as a paranoia hedge against Error-class throws between L36 and L37.` This documents the actual defensive scope honestly so a future maintainer doesn't restructure on a wrong premise.

findings.issue: Race-condition test uses `ConcurrencyTestUtils.parallelInvoke(2, ...)` correctly and asserts both statuses are 200 + single row + single ENQUEUED. However, it does NOT assert the duplicate counter ticked exactly once — `assertThat(counter("duplicate")).isEqualTo(1.0);` would prove the self-heal branch fired (only one of the two requests should hit DuplicateKey). Without this, a regression where both requests succeeded via separate Mongo inserts (e.g. unique index dropped) would still pass: single row could mean 'index works and the test happened to serialize' OR 'index is gone but both inserts collapsed to one document due to MongoDB upsert semantics'. The counter assertion makes the failure mode unambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Add `assertThat(counter("duplicate")).as("exactly one of the two parallel POSTs must hit the self-heal branch").isEqualTo(1.0);` after `awaitEnqueuedCount(1L);` on line 272. This pins that the (projectId, updateId) unique index fired AND the catch(DuplicateKeyException) branch executed for one of the two parallel requests.
